title: init & clone
subtitle: Start a new repo or copy an existing one
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: You either start a new project from scratch or join an existing one. In both cases, you need a local Git repository to start tracking changes.
whyItExists.solution: git init creates a new empty repo in any folder. git clone downloads a copy of an existing remote repo (from GitHub or anywhere).
whyItExists.whenToUse: init for brand new projects. clone for any existing GitHub repo — open-source projects, team repos, or your own repos on a new machine.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't run git init inside an existing Git repo (nested repos create complex situations). Check with git status first.

explainModes.beginner: git init tells Git to start watching a folder. git clone downloads a project from GitHub to your computer so you can work on it locally.
explainModes.simple: git init — creates a .git hidden folder in your current directory, making it a Git repo. git clone <url> — downloads a full copy of a remote repo including all history. Both give you a local repo to work in.
explainModes.standard: git init sets up a local repo from scratch. git clone does three things: fetches the remote, sets up tracking branches, and checks out the default branch. After cloning, origin is automatically set as the remote name for the source URL.
explainModes.technical: git init creates the .git directory with HEAD, config, description, hooks/, info/, objects/, and refs/. git clone --bare creates a repo without a working tree — used for server-side repos. git clone --depth 1 creates a shallow clone with only the most recent commit — faster for CI but lacks history.
explainModes.deepDive: The .git directory is the entire repository — delete it and you lose all history. git init --separate-git-dir moves .git to another location, useful for tracking dotfiles. git clone supports multiple transport protocols: https://, git://, ssh://, and file://. SSH cloning is more secure for private repos. The git bundle command creates a single-file transportable repo snapshot for airgapped environments.

content.text: git init — start tracking a folder

content.code:
# Navigate to your project folder
cd my-project

# Initialise a Git repository
git init
# → Initialized empty Git repository in /path/to/my-project/.git/

# OR create a new folder and init in one step
git init my-new-project
cd my-new-project

# See the hidden .git folder (use -a to show hidden files)
ls -a
# → .  ..  .git

content.text: The .git folder is Git's database — it stores your entire history. Don't delete or edit it manually.
git clone — download an existing repo

content.code:
# Clone from GitHub (HTTPS — easier for beginners)
git clone https://github.com/prashantkeshr/KERNAL.git

# Clone from GitHub (SSH — more secure, no password prompts)
git clone git@github.com:prashantkeshr/KERNAL.git

# Clone into a specific folder name
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git my-folder

# Shallow clone — only last 1 commit (faster for large repos)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/user/repo.git

# After cloning:
cd KERNAL
git remote -v    # shows the 'origin' remote was set up automatically

# 1. Create folder and init
mkdir my-website && cd my-website
git init

# 2. Create your first file
echo '# My Website' > README.md

# 3. Stage and commit (covered next lesson)
git add README.md
git commit -m "Initial commit"

# 4. Create a repo on GitHub, then add it as remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourname/my-website.git

# 5. Push
git push -u origin main

questions.question: What does git clone do?
options: Downloads a full copy of a remote repository including all history
Copies files from one folder to another
questions.explanation: git clone downloads the entire repository (all commits, all branches) from a remote URL to your local machine, and automatically sets 'origin' as the remote name.

questions.question: Where does Git store the repository's data?
questions.explanation: The .git hidden folder in your project root contains the entire repository database — all commits, branches, config, and objects. Deleting it removes all history.

faq.q: What is the difference between HTTPS and SSH cloning?
faq.a: HTTPS (https://github.com/...) is simpler — use your GitHub username and a personal access token as the password. SSH (git@github.com:...) uses a key pair stored on your machine — more secure and no password prompts once set up. SSH is recommended for developers who push often.

faq.q: Can I accidentally overwrite an existing repo with git init?
faq.a: Running git init in an already-tracked folder is safe — it just re-initializes. It won't delete history. But avoid running it inside another repo's subfolder unless you intentionally want a submodule.

examples: Your first day at a new job: git clone https://github.com/company/main-app.git
Contributing to open-source: fork on GitHub, then git clone your fork
Backing up a local project: git init, then push to a new GitHub repo
